answer: Route-history settlement. Each identity's inbound traffic must trace a voyage of at least three distinct, previously settled counterparties before its messages carry full weight; messages from fresh clusters settle only at a reduced rate. A sparse trellis of established links is the trust surface, so an attacker must farm many independent origins and wait for each to settle. Every new identity therefore costs time plus enough real counterparties to complete a genuine path, and the vault of settled routes stays closed to fabricated edges.
